articles.title_zh: Rare September Nor’easter set to slam East Coast with heavy rain, damaging winds
articles.content_orig:
BREAKING: CNN, MS NOW and Politico allowed back onto the White House grounds after a judge ordered Trump to lift his ban
Millions across the Northeast are bracing for an intense, multi-day Nor’easter this weekend that is forecast to bring heavy rain and strong wind gusts to the East Coast.
Forecast models still disagree on the storm’s exact track, but one thing is clear: wherever it goes, it will hit the region hard. Forecasters have high confidence in a long-duration onshore wind event that could bring significant coastal flooding.
Coastal flood warnings and high wind watches are already in place along much of the East Coast, with more alerts likely to be issued throughout the day Thursday.
The highest rainfall totals — 2 to 3 inches or more — are most likely from Rhode Island to eastern Massachusetts.
Powerful winds, including gusts up to 50-60 mph, risk toppling power lines and trees. Small shifts in the storm’s track will determine where outages and downed trees are most likely to occur.
Coastal flooding is expected to run 1 to 3 feet above high tide, and a full moon Saturday night could intensify the tides and worsen the flooding. Waves along the coast are expected to reach 12 feet in Ocean City, New Jersey, and up to 22 feet in New England.
Moderate to major flooding is likely from North Carolina to Nantucket, Massachusetts, with southeastern Virginia — particularly the Virginia Beach-to-Norfolk area — at highest risk for major coastal inundation of 1 to 3 feet.
Meanwhile, a separate storm is already pummeling the Eastern Seaboard, generating high winds and rough surf.
In Massachusetts, residents were seen this week hauling their boats out of the bay, worried about high tides and flooding from the Nor’easter. One person told NBC News he’d been “prepping all week for both wind and water.”
One couple even changed their wedding plans because of the storm — they had been set to marry this weekend on a Massachusetts beach.
And the Boston Red Sox moved Sunday’s game — the season finale — up to Friday to avoid any weather-related delays or cancellations.
In New Jersey, crews cleared debris from storm drains and flood-prone areas as emergency management officials urged residents to prepare for the incoming storm. Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden recommended charging devices and stocking up on batteries ahead of possible power outages.
Elsewhere in the country, days of heavy rain in the Southwest have triggered major flooding, sending muddy waters sweeping through the streets of New Mexico. The El Paso, Texas, fire department said it has responded to more than 50 storm-related calls.
Off the coast of Hawaii’s Big Island, Tropical Storm Nolo threatens heavy rain and flash flooding, with more than 30 inches of rain  possible in some areas. Extreme rainfall remains the storm’s biggest risk.
Nolo currently has sustained winds of 50 mph and is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Thursday night — potentially reaching Category 3 strength. As of the latest update, the storm was about 285 miles south of South Point, Hawaii, moving north at 2 mph.
Nolo is not expected to make direct landfall in Hawaii, but it could come close enough to bring tropical-storm-force winds to the Big Island and Maui as early as Thursday night, with hurricane-force winds possible by Friday night.

Sam Brock is an NBC News correspondent.

She was previously denied access despite multiple attempts to enter the White House on Thursday morning.

Federal Judge Timothy Kelly has ordered the Trump administration to respond imminently to the concerns from news outlets whose reporters, previously banned from the White House by Trump, were again denied access this morning after Kelly ordered their access be restored.
With both China and the US leading the world in AI development, Xi Jinping told reporters at the White House that both nations have the capability and responsibility to manage AI for good, and “ensure the development of AI is always under human control and serve the wellbeing of the people”.
Shortly after Xi Jinping’s arrival at the White House, Donald Trump gave remarks alongside the visiting Chinese president, in which the two expressed optimism for deepening the testy US-China relationship.
Trump, speaking, noted that Xi is the first Chinese leader to make a second formal visit to the White House, and said the two have “forged a truly great friendship” since Trump was first elected in 2016.
Trump went on to say that he’s “very proud” of the US-China relationship, and says the two countries are working towards a “more balanced trade relationship.” He said the two leaders will also discuss “pressing issues” concerning security, technology and artificial intelligence.
“The decisions we make in these areas today can promote peace and prosperity for decades and decades to come,” Trump said.
Taking to the podium after him, Xi said both China and the United States are “great countries” with “great peoples,” and that he came to Washington to “carry on our friendship, expand co-operation and promote the wellbeing of both our peoples”.
He added that China and the US “shoulder a responsibility to promote human progress” and said he is willing to work with Trump to “steer the ship of China-US ties”.
“The interests of China and the United States are deeply intertwined,” Xi said, adding that it would be hard to solve many of the world’s problems without the two countries co-operating with one another.
Xi then issued an invitation for 100,000 American students to visit China in the next five years, and announced that two pandas – Ping Ping and Fu Shuang – will settle into their new home at the Atlanta zoo in the coming days. The move is reminiscent of China’s gift of two giant pandas to the Smithsonian national zoo in 1972, following Richard Nixon’s historic visit to Beijing in the detente era of the Cold War.
To the blare of trumpets, Donald Trump and first lady Melania Trump walked out of the White House residence onto the South Lawn, where they greeted Xi Jinping and his wife Peng Liyuan as they stepped out of a black vehicle and onto the red carpet.
They warmly shook hands and then posed for the cameras.
Anti-Beijing and pro-Beijing protesters gathered outside the White House ahead of Xi’s arrival, the Associated Press notes.
“Down with Xi Jinping ,” chanted those condemning Beijing’s brutal policy in Tibet . They also chanted, “Shame on Xi Jinping.”
Another group has gathered about a block away with banners welcoming the Chinese leader.
The two camps are separated and there has been no direct clash.

“This morning journalists from each of CNN, MS NOW, and POLITICO attempted to enter the White House and were turned away, and Secret Service agents confiscated the hard pass of journalists whose hard passes had not previously been confiscated,” a new court filing read.
Time, the request continued, is “of the essence. CNN is scheduled to the television pool this evening for President Xi Jinping’s visit to the White House.”
Timothy Kelly, the federal judge, a Trump appointee who ruled in favor of a CNN journalist similarly barred from the White House during Trump’s first term, issued an order last night ordering the Trump administration to restore access to the three outlets while their case proceeds.

Week 4 is the biggest weekend of the 2026 college football season.
Saturday features six matchups between teams ranked in the AP Top 25. Four of those come in the SEC and the other two are in the Big Ten. We won't filibuster any longer. Here are the games to watch this weekend.
The winner gets to be called UT for the rest of the year. The loser has to find another acronym.
It's the biggest game of young Tennessee QB Faizon Brandon's career and he's shown why he won the starting QB job as a true freshman through the first three games. Brandon has yet to throw an interception and has nine total touchdowns; he's thrown for six and rushed for three.
Two of those games have come against Furman and Kennesaw State , so it's hard to judge just how good the Volunteers offense actually is this season. But it's a promising sign that Tennessee has been able to dominate its opponents on the ground no matter who it has played. In a 45-24 win over Georgia Tech , the Vols rushed 45 times for 299 yards.
That takes pressure off Brandon; he was 10-of-21 passing for 148 yards and two scores against the Yellow Jackets. Is that run game sustainable against the Longhorns? Teams are averaging just 3.4 yards a carry against Texas this season and Ohio State had 94 yards on 31 carries.
Auburn transfer Cam Coleman hasn't caught more than four passes in a game so far the season for Texas, but he's scored twice against both Texas State and UTSA. Arch Manning is averaging under seven yards an attempt through the first three games of the season and Tennessee's opponents have thrown for just 453 yards all season.
The Rebels' status as an underdog isn't a sign of disrespect to a top-five team. Rather, it's more about how good Florida has looked through the first three weeks of Jon Sumrall's tenure.
The Gators were the clear better team in their win over Auburn as Jadan Baugh has established himself as one of the best running backs in the country. Baugh has 458 yards and eight touchdowns already this season and is averaging 8.5 yards every time he carries the ball. Teams haven't been afraid to run the ball against Ole Miss so far this season, either. Charlotte's 33 attempts are the fewest of any Ole Miss opponent and LSU rushed for 172 yards and two scores in the Rebels' 32-24 win in Week 3.
It's also a potential letdown spot for Ole Miss. The game against LSU was such a focal point since the schedule was released that it's only natural to think the Rebels won't be as up for this game. Will that be rooted in any basis in reality? We'll know on Saturday.
We may also need to wait until Saturday to know about Ole Miss RB Kewan Lacy 's status. He re-injured his surgically repaired left shoulder in the win over LSU and missed the end of the game. JT Lindsey was effective in Lacy's absence, but Ole Miss is a much better football team with its star on the field. Having Lacy out there and effective helps Trinidad Chambliss share the playmaking burden.
This game has all the potential in the world to satiate your desires for old-school football. The over/under of 38.5 is the lowest of any game offered at BetMGM in Week 4.
No one is giving up fewer points per game than Iowa through three weeks. The Hawkeyes have shut out Northern Illinois and Northern Iowa — at least Michigan doesn't have "north" in its name — and allowed 13 points to Iowa State in Week 2. Those three teams have put up just 177 yards per game.
Hank Brown has taken over as Iowa's starting quarterback after a competition with Jeremy Hecklinski that went all the way to Week 1. The former Auburn QB is 45-of-62 passing for 473 yards and three touchdowns. Those are explosive numbers compared to the passing offense that Iowa has had in recent seasons.
The biggest question may actually come at running back, where both Kamari Moulton and L.J. Phillips missed the Week 3 win. Moulton and Phillips are the Hawkeyes' top running backs. Iowa didn't need them against its FCS foe, but will need at least one available on Saturday.
Michigan's offense finally broke free in the second half of a 52-17 win over UTEP in Week 3. After scoring 30 points over the first two weeks of the season, the Wolverines nearly matched that number with four touchdowns in the third quarter alone.
Will that game be a turning point for an offense that had looked stuck for the better part of 10 quarters? There are few questions about the Michigan defense. The ceiling for the Wolverines will be entirely determined by just how good the offense can be.
Some of the luster disappeared from this game as both teams lost in Week 3. Texas A&M's home loss to Kentucky was entirely unexpected. And it wasn't a fluke, either. The Wildcats bossed the Aggies .
Texas A&M lost receiver Terry Bussey for the season with a right leg injury on the opening kickoff. That puts more pressure on Mario Craver and Isaiah Horton to be the primary playmakers for an Aggies passing game that looks to need a robust support system around quarterback Marcel Reed . Craver and Horton have combined to catch 31 of the 62 completions Reed has thrown this season and all but one of his touchdown passes.
Reed emerged as Texas A&M's quarterback in this game two seasons ago as he came off the bench to rush for three scores in a 38-23 win. This season, he's completing less than 60% of his passes.
Sam Leavitt is still looking for his first great game as LSU's starting quarterback. Leavitt has thrown at least one interception in each of the Tigers' first three games and has five interceptions to just three touchdown passes. He's supplemented that total with six rushing touchdowns, but Leavitt needs to be a better passer for the Tigers' playoff hopes to become reality.
And the playoff is going to be a central theme of this game. The loser will drop to 2-2 and likely have no path to the postseason with another loss.
This is another game with some serious playoff implications, especially for an Oregon team that already has a loss thanks to that Week 2 defeat at Oklahoma State.
Even if it'd be a victory over a .500 Oregon team, a win would be a defining one for this Big Ten version of USC. The Trojans haven't threatened to be in the top tier of the conference since making the move from the Pac-12. Yes, there was a home win over Michigan in 2025, but that Wolverines team finished with five losses.
As always, there are still questions about the USC defense. The Trojans shut out Fresno State in a dominant Week 1 performance. But they've otherwise allowed 26 points in each of the other three games and 75 points combined over the past two weeks. The 35 points Rutgers scored in Week 3 was just seven fewer than the Scarlet Knights ' combined total over the first two weeks of the season.
If Oregon's offense has the same tells that it allegedly did against Oklahoma State, former TCU coach Gary Patterson's unit can tee off. But if the Portland State game was some much-needed corrective action, the Ducks could easily be the third straight team to drop 30 or more against the Trojans. If that happens and USC still wins, QB Jayden Maiava is going to get a lot of Heisman love. Through four games, Maiava is completing 76% of his passes for 1,173 yards and 12 TDs to just one interception.
Clemson (1-) at Cal (10:30 p.m. ET Friday, ESPN): We've got some serious ACC-after-dark potential with this one. Cal CB Kingston Lopa added a fifth interception against Wagner in Week 3 and will be licking his chops at the prospect of facing freshman Tait Reynolds in his first road start. Reynolds was much better after Clemson's win over North Carolina resumed following a lengthy weather delay.

articles.title_zh: Chinese analysts say Trump should "understand pressure doesn't work," as he and Xi tackle thorny issues
articles.content_orig:
Hong Kong — It was 11 years ago that Chinese President Xi Jinping last visited the U.S. capital, for a 2015 White House meeting with then-President Barack Obama. As he returns for a meeting on Thursday with President Trump , both Xi and China's role in the world have changed dramatically.
China is now regarded as America's chief geopolitical rival, and Xi arrived back in Washington Wednesday night projecting confidence and authority.
"I think after all these years, Americans should understand pressure doesn't work," Dr. Zhao Hai, an expert in Sino-U.S. relations and vice president of the Chinese Institute of Hong Kong, told CBS News ahead of the leaders' summit in Washington. "It doesn't work on Xi. It doesn't work on China, and it doesn't work on the Chinese people."
When President Trump visited Beijing in May, he and Xi agreed to pursue what they called "constructive strategic stability" — political-speak indicating a commitment to improve the world's most important bilateral relationship despite deep mistrust, suspicion and intense competition.
Four months later, Chinese analysts see little reason to hope for any major breakthroughs, and they say the bilateral relationship, far from easing, appears as strained as ever.
Xi will be keen to secure an extension of the fragile economic truce that has walked the world's two biggest economies back from last year's damaging trade war.
In late 2025, Mr. Trump backed down from threats to impose 100% tariffs on some Chinese imports after Beijing threatened to limit supplies of vital rare earth materials.
Later agreements reached during the summit in May, on the sale of U.S. soybeans, other agricultural products and Boeing aircraft to China, are likely to come up.
Beijing insists the relationship cannot be one-sided, and Xi is likely to push Mr. Trump to open up the U.S. market to more Chinese goods, potentially to Chinese electric vehicles .
In 2015, Xi traveled to the U.S. with the leaders of 15 Chinese companies, including Jack Ma, the boss of online retail giant Alibaba, and executives from tech giants Tencent and Baidu.
Professor Wu Xinbo, who advises China's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, told CBS News he believed Xi had intended to bring a similar contingent with him to Washington this week, but that the U.S. did not approve visas for some Chinese business leaders ahead of the trip.
As a result, Wu said China decided not to send a business delegation this week. China's state television network CCTV listed the members of Xi's entourage, and it included his wife and a number of high-ranking Chinese Communist Party officials, but no corporate leaders.
Safety concerns over the breakneck pace of artificial intelligence advancement are also expected to feature prominently in the leaders' discussion, following warnings from industry leaders that the technology could pose an existential threat to humanity .
Many Chinese firms agree that AI must be regulated, according to Leia Wang, a non-resident scholar at the Carnegie Endowment for Peace, told CBS News recently.
Yi Zeng, the dean of the Beijing Institute of AI Safety and Governance, wrote in a research paper shared with CBS News, meanwhile, that "the catastrophic risks posed by AI, and the hidden danger of human extinction, are growing by the day."
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, who has spoken out against regulating AI development, said in April that it was essential for U.S. and Chinese researchers to engage in dialogue, and he warned that such bilateral coordination by AI industry leaders " is glaringly missing because of the current [U.S.] attitude about China as an adversary ."
Zhao also questioned Washington's commitment to engage in any genuine cooperation with its strategic competitors.
"This is not an American issue or a Chinese issue, this is a humankind issue, and it's very threatening," he told CBS News, adding that, in his view, "the Chinese government is much more concerned about the negative side of AI development and has more measures and tools to regulate AI development ."
President Trump made it clear just before his meeting with Xi that he was not in favor of any guardrails on AI development despite concerns about the possible emergence of superintelligence - a theoretical AI agent smarter than any person — and he said China's leader was in agreement.
"Super Intelligence (SI) will be a big topic of discussion, but I want to leave it exactly where it is. That is China's position also. Our guardrail is the DOJ," Mr. Trump said in a social media post.
Xi is expected to press President Trump to limit U.S. support for Taiwan — the Chinese leader's top priority. He's widely expected to urge Mr. Trump to halt all arms sales to the self-governed island and oppose Taiwanese independence.
That would effectively end the longstanding policy of refusing to state whether the U.S. would intervene militarily if China were to attack Taiwan, a practice known as "strategic ambiguity."
After their last summit in May, President Trump said he had made "no commitment either way" on whether to move forward with a pending arms sale to the island. Democratic and Republican lawmakers urged the arms package to be approved, but it has remained in limbo since Trump and Xi last met.
Mr. Trump, who has rejected multiple reports that Beijing supports Iran in its ongoing war with the U.S., is expected to again seek Xi's assistance in resolving the conflict and ensuring the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. How he does that could determine the outcome, according to Zhao.
"If the American side is only thinking about pressuring China, and particularly using financial tools to pressure China, I think that will be a deal breaker," he told CBS News.
"We should not be too ambitious about this trip," added Wu, calling the bilateral meeting taking place at all an achievement, given the two nations' differences.
Wu attributed the lack of progress on the key issues thus far, in part, to what he called a big disconnect between what Mr. Trump says, and what his administration actually does.
He pointed, as examples, to the Pentagon placing 54 Chinese companies on a blacklist over the last two months; the Department of Homeland Security placing Chinese universities (including the one where Wu teaches) and other institutions on a watchlist , and the Federal Communications Commission imposed new regulations on Chinese robotics and other electronics.
Those measures were taken "all to gain leverage for these talks," Wu argued. "So, basically, beneath the surface, this relationship is far from stable."

articles.title_zh: Judge temporarily overturns Trump's White House media ban
articles.content_orig:
CNN White House reporter Betsy Klein was reportedly denied access on Thursday
Three US media outlets have requested an emergency court hearing, accusing the White House of having "repeatedly violated" a judge's order to restore their access in a stand-off with President Donald Trump.
Employees from CNN, Politico and MS Now reported being denied entry on Thursday morning, with some having their credentials confiscated, while others were granted access.
Judge Timothy Kelly ruled in the early hours of Thursday that Trump's ban on the outlets should be temporarily lifted because it "likely violated their constitutional due process rights".
Trump initially said he banned the outlets because of "fake news". The White House later cited national security.
It was unclear whether the refusal to admit some reporters on Thursday morning was because of an administrative lag as the White House potentially worked to comply with the judge's order.
The standoff was expected to impact TV coverage as Trump welcomes Chinese President Xi Jinping to the White House on Thursday morning ahead of a state dinner.
CNN said some of their journalists had been denied entry, including senior White House reporter Betsy Klein. But a producer was allowed to enter, the outlet reported.
Politico said one of its reporters was denied access to the White House and had his press credentials confiscated.
MS NOW reported that its White House reporter Laura BarrÃ³n-LÃ³pez and a producer were barred and had their passes taken, but another MS NOW producer was allowed in.
The White House is yet to comment on the ruling, and lawyers acting for the president may take further legal action.
Trump first announced last Friday he was barring the three major US media outlets - CNN, MS Now and Politico - from the White House, accusing them of writing "fiction or lies" about his administration.
By Saturday morning, each outlet reported that they were denied entry to the White House grounds and that their press badges were confiscated.
All three outlets spoke out against the ban, accusing the Trump administration of violating their constitutional rights.
In a joint statement on Monday, they said they were pursuing legal action to "defend the principle that the government does not decide what the press reports".
Most other major media outlets have stood behind the three outlets in their fight against Trump's ban, with TV networks including Fox News, NBC, CBS and ABC suspending their televised coverage of the White House in solidarity.
And more than 50 media organisations across the ideological spectrum filed an amicus brief in support of the lawsuit, including Fox News, The New York Times, The Washington Post and The Wall Street Journal.
There have been previous instances of administrations attempting to limit certain outlets' access.
The Obama administration tried to exclude Fox News from participating in a specific press pool interview with an administration official in 2009.
But after objections from the other four networks in the pool, Fox News was allowed in.

articles.title_orig: Google Is Sending an A.I. Data Center to Outer Space
articles.title_zh: Google Is Sending an A.I. Data Center to Outer Space
articles.content_orig:
Google is taking its first step toward making Project Suncatcher a reality. Announced last year, Suncatcher is Google’s “moonshot” effort to design orbital AI data centers, which AI boosters like Elon Musk and Jeff Bezos have pitched as an alternative to divisive terrestrial data centers . Google’s first experimental satellite will launch on October 1 with the aim of validating Google’s vision for a constellation of AI satellites .
The satellite, dubbed MVP, is about the size of a refrigerator. Inside, it has four of Google’s custom TPU AI accelerators, which are used to train AI models and run inference to generate tokens for AI workloads. On Earth, a data center will run thousands of these chips, which consume massive amounts of power—one of the reasons putting solar-powered AI hardware in space is so attractive.
MVP is starting small, with solar panels that supply only about one kilowatt of power, The New York Times reports. That’s enough to power a microwave or a hair dryer. Google did not build the satellite from scratch. While the AI hardware inside is Google’s, the spacecraft comes from a satellite imagery firm called Planet Labs. The initial plan was to launch two custom satellites in 2027, but Google wanted to accelerate its efforts. So the company opted to integrate its chips into a satellite that Planet Labs had already built for an early test.
Google’s AI test will launch as part of the upcoming Transporter-18 rideshare aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket. Eventually, Google wants to have networks of orbiting satellites that communicate over high-speed laser connections, probably requiring expensive dedicated launched. This lone satellite will serve as a test of several technologies and will operate for just a few months.
Google says it has conducted testing on the ground, but launching the satellite will provide a fuller picture of the current challenges. For example, the team will need to evaluate how Tensor chips handle space conditions. In many space missions, hardware is designed specifically for extreme temperatures or radiation, but these are the same TPUs that Google integrates into servers on the ground. Radiation can damage chips or simply interfere with calculations by flipping bits. But vibration and high g-forces during launch also pose problems. Still, as we’ve seen with missions like the Ingenuity Mars helicopter , off-the-shelf hardware can hold up pretty well out there.
Cooling the chips may be the biggest issue , something many observers have pointed out as the AI industry has gone wild over the idea of orbital data centers. Radiator systems exist in space, but they’re designed to remove a relatively small amount of heat. AI accelerators generate far more heat by comparison. Google’s solution uses a layer of malleable “thermal interface material” that connects the chips to aluminum and copper heat pipes. Those components conduct heat into a radiator that can project it into space.
Google will run Gemini models on the TPUs for testing, but they won’t be able to run continuously. The cooling system will only be able to operate in brief spurts of about 15 minutes. After that, the TPUs need to shut down to allow the radiators to catch up.
With this first test, Google hopes to understand what does and doesn’t work, allowing it to improve its designs for future missions. The 2027 launches are still on the agenda, but the team expects it will be years before Suncatcher evolves from “project” to “product.”

A stabbing at a Catholic convent in Poland on Thursday left one person dead and four others wounded, authorities said.
Police detained a suspect following the incident in a southeastern town in Poland.
Police said they were made aware of the stabbing on the grounds of the Benedictine Sisters monastery on the ground of the abbey in Jarosław at around 9.30 am local time (0730 GMT). Four men and a woman were stabbed.
The victims were rushed to a hospital, with three of the men suffering serious injuries. Police later confirmed that one of the men had died, Polish news agency PAP reported.
"We know that the act was committed by a 31-year-old Ukrainian national who had entered Poland from Germany earlier today," said Bozena Harasz-Woloszyn from the District Prosecutor's Office in Przemysl.
Harasz-Woloszyn added that the attacker used a knife he took from a kitchen on the premises to attack four men and one woman, including one priest who was in a confessional.
"Three of the victims are clergy members and two are laypeople; one person has died," she said. "Two people are in a critical, life-threatening condition."
"We are aware that Father Stanislaw has passed away and Father Marek is in serious condition; there are other casualties, but we do not have further details," Sister Barbara Dendor told state broadcaster TVP Info.
"When I arrived, there was total panic; young people who had come out of the center witnessed it — they were saying, 'Some madman, some madman!'" she said.
The mayor of Jaroslaw, Marcin Nazarewicz, told a press conference that a period of mourning was being declared until the end of the week.
"We are aware that Father Stanisław has passed away and Father Marek is in serious condition; there are other casualties, but we do not have further details," Sister Barbara Dendor told state broadcaster TVP Info.

Oracle shares fell 5% on Thursday following news that the company sent a "force majeure" notice tied to its New Mexico data center project to protect itself from higher expenses.
"Project Jupiter remains on our planned schedule," an Oracle said in a statement to CNBC. "We are fully committed to New Mexico and confident in our path forward."
Bloomberg was first to report the news, citing sources familiar with the matter.
The company is looking to delay payment on the campus, dubbed Project Jupiter, if it doesn't come online as expected in 2028, according to the report.
Oracle sent the notice to the developer, which is a unit of Blue Owl Capital , CNBC confirmed. Blue Owl also saw its shares fall on Thursday.
"This notice does not change the financial commitments to this multi-year project," Blue Owl Capital said in a statement to CNBC.
The New Mexico data center project, which is part of the broader Stargate artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout with President Donald Trump , has been riddled with setbacks and regulatory hurdles.
That includes local opposition to data centers ahead of the upcoming midterm elections and concerns from environmental groups.
Co-CEO Clay Magouyrk told analysts on the company's earnings call on Sept. 10 that Project Jupiter would not affect its previously stated fiscal 2027 revenue or earnings guidance.
Concerns have also mounted over Oracle's $18 billion in debt tied to the datacenter, which is already trading at stressed levels, according to the Financial Times.

We’re living under a dark cloud, with a steady downpour of graft, thuggery and baloney.
There’s the raffling of presidential pardons and the attacks on reporters for doing their jobs, the clownish trade war with Canada, the bungled disaster in Iran, the  petty obsessions with the ballroom and the Kennedy Center, the hogwash about a stolen election, the attacks on immigrants and the shameless presidential profiteering while working people suffer the cost of Trump’s countless broken promises.
I could go on, and I will. But rest assured, I have not forgotten about the boost I promised.
For all the affronts, nothing strikes me as more sinister than the Trump administration’s ambitious assault on the planet . Despite nearly daily headlines about the global calamity of overheated oceans, melting glaciers, stark weather transformations and species extinction, Trump keeps shoveling more coal onto a fire that will rage long after he’s dead and gone.
He’s gutted environmental protections and scientific research and  dismantled clean energy initiatives. Now his administration is rolling back limits on power plant emissions, attempting to open the California coast to more oil drilling and sabotaging the state’s ambitious goals on emission controls and electric vehicle conversion.
We don’t need AI to threaten the future of humanity. We’ve got Trump.
It’s tempting to duck under the covers and wait for the nightmare to end, but the good news is that a lot of people are standing up rather than rolling over, rebelling against the ignorance and callous disregard that threatens our most precious and fragile shared inheritance.
In August, hundreds showed up to defend California’s authority to govern its own coast at a Santa Monica hearing of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Agency, and 18,000 more people filed comments online.
‘It is not the job of the people of California to compensate for Trump’s financial losses,’ writes an L.A. Times reader.
The rollback of environmental safeguards is, for many, a call to arms.
“Yes, I am discouraged. … But I am not despairing,” said Bill McKibben , an author and environmental activist who is organizing a worldwide event called Sun Day for next year to promote clean energy. “We’re reacting to multiple crises, and we’re led by a pack of fools, so why would anybody not stand up?”
McKibben launched a national movement five years ago called Third Act, and tens of thousands of people 60 and older have signed on to advocate for climate action, voting rights and civic participation. Third Act now operates in about 30 states, with a robust chapter in Southern California.
Former Times reporter Zan Dubin has worked as both a volunteer and a paid communications consultant for Third Act, and I asked her what someone could expect to do if they became a member of Third Act/SoCal .
“We do it all,” Dubin said, from promoting climate-friendly candidates to running phone banks and testifying at public meetings. She said Third Act co-sponsors protests at Dodger Stadium, and she and others planned to meet at Vin Scully Avenue and Stadium Way for Sunday’s game against the San Francisco Giants. They want the Dodgers to stop doing business with Big Oil and bench their sponsorship deal with Phillips 66.
She also called out Disneyland for its exhaust-spewing Autopia attraction, along with former Times climate columnist Sammy Roth, and Disneyland responded by announcing in 2024 that it was switching to electric cars beginning in 2027.
Dubin, co-founder of National Drive Electric Week , said 170 volunteer-led events were being held nationwide over the next month to promote EVs, and she was leading one Friday in Irvine.
“Action is absolutely the antidote to despair,” Dubin said. “I find that despite the onslaught of these horrifying headlines … taking action invigorates me.”
Claremont resident Margaret Davis knows that feeling. She emailed me in 2023, prior to participating in a Third Act event, and said many retirees have time on their hands, which puts them in a powerful position.
“The climate crisis is the greatest existential threat humans have ever faced, hence we live in a time when we can make the greatest change for the better,” Davis wrote at the time.
When I called her a few days ago, Davis told me she’s now a member of Senior Stewards Acting for the Environment . She lives at Pilgrim Place — a senior community with a focus on justice, peace and environment — where residents meet regularly to study, discuss and advocate for sustainability, biodiversity and environmental causes.
As legislative session closed, Newsom pushed environmental break for donor.
“When I was in college in 1970, we had the antiwar movement and that was the first year of Earth Day,” Davis said. “At the time, I thought Earth Day was just a distraction from what was going on in the world.”
Later, she said, “I came to realize it was the biggest issue of all time.”
Like Davis, I went to college in the ‘70s, and there’s no denying that our aggressively consumptive generation played a key role in manufacturing a crisis for our children and grandchildren. We’ve got matches in our hands and smoke on the horizon, and if we’re honest with ourselves, we’d see atonement not as a hobby, but as a duty.
As for the next generation, climate activist Sim Bilal, 24, said  he too shares the sense that this is both a wickedly frightening time and a moment of opportunity.
“In the last month, we’ve gotten more young people involved,” said Bilal, executive director of Youth Climate Stewards 4 Local Action . “We usually have to reach out to them, but so many people have been wanting to get involved, and they’re so eager, and that’s been affirming for me. The policies are depressing, but the fact that people are reenergized and want to fight back is really exciting.”
Bilal said faith in politics, government and corporations is not high among his peers, but he’s trying to grow a network of young people to cultivate and support future leaders.
“A mentor told me there are two kinds of power — organized people, and organized money,” said Bilal, whose activism began when his grandmother died  and he began wondering if her cancer, and global warming, were connected to  the oil drilling in his South L.A. neighborhood. “We don’t have the money, but a lot of the work we do is political and civic education, demystifying power, and making people understand they have agency.”
You needed a boost, right?
Whatever your age, do not despair.

Millions across the Northeast are bracing for an intense, multi-day Nor’easter this weekend that is forecast to bring heavy rain and strong wind gusts to the East Coast.
Forecast models still disagree on the storm’s exact track, but one thing is clear: wherever it goes, it will hit the region hard. Forecasters have high confidence in a long-duration onshore wind event that could bring significant coastal flooding.
Coastal flood warnings and high wind watches are already in place along much of the East Coast, with more alerts likely to be issued throughout the day Thursday.
The highest rainfall totals — 2 to 3 inches or more — are most likely from Rhode Island to eastern Massachusetts.
Powerful winds, including gusts up to 50-60 mph, risk toppling power lines and trees. Small shifts in the storm’s track will determine where outages and downed trees are most likely to occur.
Coastal flooding is expected to run 1 to 3 feet above high tide, and a full moon Saturday night could intensify the tides and worsen the flooding. Waves along the coast are expected to reach 12 feet in Ocean City, New Jersey, and up to 22 feet in New England.
Moderate to major flooding is likely from North Carolina to Nantucket, Massachusetts, with southeastern Virginia — particularly the Virginia Beach-to-Norfolk area — at highest risk for major coastal inundation of 1 to 3 feet.
Meanwhile, a separate storm is already pummeling the Eastern Seaboard, generating high winds and rough surf.
In Massachusetts, residents were seen this week hauling their boats out of the bay, worried about high tides and flooding from the Nor’easter. One person told NBC News he’d been “prepping all week for both wind and water.”
One couple even changed their wedding plans because of the storm — they had been set to marry this weekend on a Massachusetts beach.
And the Boston Red Sox moved Sunday’s game — the season finale — up to Friday to avoid any weather-related delays or cancellations.
In New Jersey, crews cleared debris from storm drains and flood-prone areas as emergency management officials urged residents to prepare for the incoming storm. Monmouth County Sheriff Shaun Golden recommended charging devices and stocking up on batteries ahead of possible power outages.
Elsewhere in the country, days of heavy rain in the Southwest have triggered major flooding, sending muddy waters sweeping through the streets of New Mexico. The El Paso, Texas, fire department said it has responded to more than 50 storm-related calls.
Off the coast of Hawaii’s Big Island, Tropical Storm Nolo threatens heavy rain and flash flooding, with more than 30 inches of rain  possible in some areas. Extreme rainfall remains the storm’s biggest risk.
Nolo currently has sustained winds of 50 mph and is expected to strengthen into a hurricane by Thursday night — potentially reaching Category 3 strength. As of the latest update, the storm was about 285 miles south of South Point, Hawaii, moving north at 2 mph.
Nolo is not expected to make direct landfall in Hawaii, but it could come close enough to bring tropical-storm-force winds to the Big Island and Maui as early as Thursday night, with hurricane-force winds possible by Friday night.

Chinese investment in the US has fallen to its lowest level since 2011 amid tighter scrutiny and trade tensions
China’s outbound direct investment reached a record high of US$214 billion last year, even as investment in the United States plunged to its lowest level in more than a decade amid growing geopolitical and regulatory uncertainty, latest official data showed.
Outbound direct investment was up 11.1 per cent in 2025 compared to the previous year, making China the world’s second-largest source of global capital, behind only the US and ranking ahead of Japan, according to an annual report jointly issued by the Ministry of Commerce and two other state economic bodies on Wednesday.
This growth was partly driven by stronger investment in technology-related industries. Investment in information transmission, software and information technology services surged 88.3 per cent to reach US$13.1 billion as Chinese companies expanded their presence in such sectors abroad.
Bucking that trend was direct investment to the US, which fell 71.3 per cent to US$1.91 billion – down sharply from about US$6.63 billion in 2024 and the lowest level since 2011. The US accounted for only 0.9 per cent of China’s total outbound direct investment in 2025, according to the report.

By JIMMY MCCLOSKEY, HEAD OF NEWS and EVE BUCKLAND
Published: 07:54 EDT, 24 September 2026 | Updated: 09:57 EDT, 24 September 2026
Taylor Swift has hinted she'll be embroiled in a fictional love triangle with two A-List stars in the video for her new single Patient Zero.
Swift, 36, was seen alongside Dakota Johnson , also 36, and Colin Farrell , 50, in the 13 second teaser screened on CBS Mornings Thursday, with the full video set to debut at the MTV Video Music Awards (VMAs) on Sunday.
The clip opens with Swift diving underwater in a black dress.
Moments later Swift is seen filmed from behind standing next to a Greek-style statue while staring out the window of a modernist concrete home.
Johnson and Farrell then make somber appearances alongside the pop superstar.
All three are seen glowering at each other while wearing smart black outfits, before two women are seen shot from behind looking at a grave in a snowy cemetery.
It is unclear if the character played by Farrell is the person who dies in the clip, although the dramatic music and storyline suggests that Swift will once again sing about being mistreated by a man.
Taylor Swift is seen in the music video for her new single Patient Zero
Swift, Dakota Johnson and Colin Farrell are seen together in a scene from Swift's new music video
Happily, the star's famously turbulent love life has now settled into a period of calm. She married Kansas City Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce, 36, at Madison Square Garden in New York City on July 3.
The lavish ceremony was attended by hundreds of A-List stars but was so shrouded in secrecy that photos of Swift and Kelce at the nuptials have yet to emerge.
Fans went wild at the new clip - even likening the cinematic teaser to steamy film Fifty Shades of Grey.
The pop icon took to Instagram this week to reveal The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore, featuring four new tracks, would be released on Friday.
Sharing a sultry new album cover snap, showing the star clad in a leggy gold dress, Swift wrote: 'About a year ago, you guys did a truly unfathomable thing. Something that completely blew my mind… You gave The Life of a Showgirl the biggest first week for an album in history.
'I took a trip to Sweden to celebrate with Max and Shellback, my two collaborators on this album. Really we just wanted to reflect and take in how grateful we were for the moment we were in, but there was a studio there and we did what we do when we feel anything at all.
'We wrote more songs. I hope you love them, because they were born out of pure gratitude for your exuberance for and celebration of the album we made. The Life of a Showgirl: The Encore including four new songs is out on Friday and available to pre-order and save now.'
The four new songs include Pink Clouding, Babylon and Cleveland!, a nod to husband Travis Kelce's Cleveland Heights, Ohio , hometown, as well as recently announced single Patient Zero.
The new extended album comes a day after Swift revealed her return to music with the release of Patient Zero.
Hollywood actress Johnson showed off her acting chops in a glamorous scene from the video
Irish acting favorite Farrell was seen in the teaser too. The storyline has yet to be revealed

Swift dazzled fans yet again on Wednesday as she announced more new music and an expanded edition of most recent album, The Life of a Showgirl
On Tuesday, Swift revealed her return to music with the release of a new single titled Patient Zero
Swift had left fans speculating she was about to drop her wedding photos when her website launched a mysterious two-hour countdown on Tuesday.
Swift, known for her previous countdowns and E aster Egg messages to fans, has shared past, similar cryptic posts eventually teasing the release of new albums, new photoshoots and limited edition merchandise.
Not content with tantalizing fans on her website, Swift also changed both her Twitter and Instagram bio to read: 'And, baby, that’s sh0w business f0r y0u' along with a fire heart, with zeros replacing the letter O.
As 2pm ET struck, Swift revealed the cover artwork for her new single, the title of which appeared to be in homage to the star being described as 'patient zero' for emotional contagion in a 2024 LA Times article.
She posted a sultry new snap, captioned: 'I’ve been impatiently waiting to tell you that my brand new single “Patient Zero” will be out on September 25 (!!!!!!!!!!!!) and it’s available to pre-order now on my website for 24 hours.'
The star left fans speculating she was about to drop her wedding photos when her website launched a mysterious two-hour countdown on Tuesday
The photos showed Swift draped in revealing black dresses, while she sported smoky eye make-up and her signature red lip, seemingly launching a new era.
Fans were able to preorder three different $3.99 versions of the track, including acoustic and piano singles.
The gothic shoot, which appeared to have taken place in a crypt, led fans to speculate that Swift's single could be from 'a sister album to the life of a showgirl and it’s the death of a showgirl.'
The Daily Mail has contacted Swift's representative for further comment – and has yet to hear back.
Ahead of the announcement, fans had quipped 'plot twist it’s taylor and trav’s wedding photos behind the countdown' and 'the countdown is for the wedding photos!!'
Others speculated Swift was set to release a deluxe version of her latest album, The Life of a Showgirl, while many said the three zeros were signifying angel numbers, signaling a 'new beginning' for the star.
Swift's last album release came in October 2025 with the release of The Life of a Showgirl, while her most recent single, I Knew It, I Knew You, from the Toy Story 5 soundtrack, topped charts in June.
Earlier this week, CBS and MTV announced that Swift will receive the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors at the 2026 VMAs.
With this recognition, Swift cements her place as the most awarded VMAs solo artist in show history. She is nominated this year for 11 awards.

articles.title_orig: Darden Restaurants stock falls as Olive Garden reports slower growth
articles.title_zh: Darden Restaurants stock falls as Olive Garden reports slower growth
articles.content_orig:
Darden Restaurants on Thursday reported quarterly earnings and revenue that narrowly missed analysts' expectations as same-store sales growth at Olive Garden slows.
Shares of the company fell 5% in premarket trading.
Here's what the company reported for the quarter ended Aug. 30 compared with what Wall Street was expecting, based on a survey of analysts by LSEG:
Darden reported fiscal first-quarter net income of $233.4 million, or $2.04 per share, down from $257.8 million, or $2.19 per share, a year earlier.
Net sales rose 5.1% to $3.20 billion.
The company's same-store sales increased 3.1% during the fiscal quarter as each of Darden's business units reported growth.
LongHorn Steakhouse was once again the top performer of the portfolio this quarter, as same-store sales rose 6.2%. The chain has overtaken Olive Garden to become Darden's top performer, although it still accounts for a smaller share of the company's overall revenue.
Olive Garden saw its same-store sales inch up 1.1%. While it is still the company's largest chain by both number of locations and sales, Olive Garden has seen its growth weaken as diners have become more choosy about their spending.
Darden's fine-dining business reported same-store sales growth of 1.6%. The segment includes chains like The Capital Grille and Ruth's Chris.
The company's remaining chains, which are grouped under its "other business" division, saw same-store sales grow 3.8% in the quarter.
Darden also reiterated its forecast for fiscal 2027. The company is projecting total sales of $13.60 billion to $13.75 billion and net earnings per share from continuing operations in a range of $11.10 to $11.35.

articles.title_zh: Venezuela‘s interim president Delcy Rodríguez promises election after Maduro ousted
articles.content_orig:
Venezuela’s interim president hails ‘historic meeting’ and does not say whether she will visit snatched predecessor
Venezuela’s interim president, Delcy Rodríguez , has celebrated a “historic” meeting with Donald Trump in New York, posing for a smiley photo with the US president, less than nine months after he ordered the abduction of her boss, Nicolás Maduro.
The former foes met at a five-star hotel a few blocks from Trump Tower in Manhattan late on Tuesday on the sidelines of the UN general assembly. The hotel is about 7 miles from the Brooklyn prison where Maduro has been held since he was snatched during a special forces raid on Caracas in January.
On the eve of Tuesday’s encounter, an American reporter asked Rodríguez if she would be visiting Maduro, under whom she served as vice-president, during her stay in New York. She did not reply.
But she did find time to meet Trump at the luxury Lotte New York Palace hotel, with the get-together seen as a key part of Rodríguez’s push for international legitimacy after years of Venezuela’s diplomatic isolation under Maduro’s dictatorship. On Wednesday she is expected to address the annual UN assembly.
“We held a historic meeting with … Donald Trump, with whom we discussed strengthening the bilateral relationship between our countries and advancing a cooperation agenda in strategic areas such as energy, mining, security and other matters of common interest,” Rodríguez wrote on Instagram, in a 133-word statement that made no mention of her incarcerated ally.
Oliver Blanco, one of Rodríguez’s top diplomats, claimed the meeting marked “a new stage of dialogue and understanding between both countries” and was “an important step toward new opportunities for our country and our people”. Blanco also posted a cheery photo in which he and Trump smiled and gave the thumbs up to the camera.
A White House aide said the meeting was also attended by top US officials including the secretary of state, Marco Rubio, and the deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller.
“It was a short meeting but it was an important meeting,” Rubio said on Wednesday, telling reporters it had focused on Venezuela’s economic recovery and political transition.
Hours earlier, Rodríguez had sat in the general assembly hall watching Trump celebrate the “massive military operation” during which Maduro – whom he called an “outlaw dictator” and “a real criminal” – was captured. “It was a war … [and] to the victor belong the spoils,” Trump bragged of the recent oil deal between the US and Venezuela, as Rodríguez appeared to wince.
Some observers also detected signs of discomfort in the body language captured in the photo of Trump and Rodríguez, who appeared to be clenching her left fist.
Some of Rodríguez’s critics in Venezuela called her treatment by Trump an unmitigated humiliation for a socialist party politician who has spent years railing against American imperialism.
After Maduro’s capture, Trump warned that Rodríguez would “pay a very big price, probably bigger than Maduro,” if she did not toe the US line. Since then, Rodríguez has made a series of concessions, including ceding control of Venezuela’s oil revenues to Washington and agreeing to a controversial 65bn-barrel oil deal that Trump on Tuesday called “the largest oil deal in history”.
One opposition figure denounced the Rodríguez-Trump meeting as an encounter between a “shameless puppet and her unscrupulous puppeteer” .
But Rodríguez has succeeded in consolidating power, with Trump seemingly more focused on gaining access to Venezuela’s natural resources than pushing for a fresh presidential election that would move the South American country back towards democracy.
Trump has repeatedly praised Rodríguez’s “fantastic” and “terrific” leadership while sidelining her main rival, the opposition leader María Corina Machado. Machado, who left Venezuela late last year to receive her Nobel peace prize in Oslo, has been unable to return and is exiled in Panama. She reportedly made three attempts to return to Venezuela this week but failed.
​Orlando Pérez, a Latin America expert from the University of North Texas at Dallas, rejected the idea that Rodríguez had been humiliated by her meeting with Trump. “It’s a huge triumph [for her]. She got the photo op she wanted. I frankly don’t think you can overestimate how important the photo op was for her,” said Pérez, who believed the image legitimised Rodríguez’s position as president and signalled that Washington was happy to keep working with her and for other leaders to engage with her.
For Trump, meeting Rodríguez was a way to show Maga voters he had “won Venezuela” by commandeering its massive oil reserves with January’s invasion. “So that picture was a win-win for Delcy and for Trump ,” Pérez added.
Before Tuesday’s tête-à-tête, the presidents of the US and Venezuela had last met in 2015, when Barack Obama and Maduro spoke briefly during a regional summit in Panama. In the decade that followed, Maduro became an international pariah as he led his country into economic chaos and increasingly authoritarian rule, and Venezuela was hit by punishing international sanctions.
At the 2015 summit, Obama conceded that the days in which “the US could meddle with impunity” in Latin America were over. But Trump has dramatically different ideas and has been forging ahead with attempts to reassert US dominance in a region it has long considered its back yard.
As well as capturing Venezuela’s government and trying to topple Cuba’s communist government by strangling its economy, Trump’s push for hegemony has also seen the US accused of trying to swing Brazil’s presidential election in favour of the far-right candidate Flávio Bolsonaro through diplomatic and economic pressure.
Addressing the UN assembly on Tuesday, the Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, hit back at such efforts, without directly citing the US. “We will not allow the enemies of democracy – internal or external – to attack the will of the people. Brazilian democracy belongs to the Brazilians,” said Lula who is facing a tough battle to win re-election in October’s vote.
“Brazil doesn’t fit into anyone’s back yard,” added Lula, who also called for elections in Venezuela. He did not meet Rodríguez during her visit to New York but said the “people of Venezuela deserve to decide their own future”.
